C0.quote: The collective decision is taken through some voting mechanism
C0.note: Divisible participatory budgeting mechanism aggregating agents' submitted budget proposals.

C1.quote: Theorem 1. The US-VCG mechanism is SDSIC.
C1.note: The main result is SDSIC (SB). Vanishing payments and the properties inherited by biased mechanisms are properties of rules (AX). Welfare maximization is WD.

C2.1.value: votes; voting profile; most preferred budget decision; type profile (as input of direct-revelation mechanism)
C2.1.quote: agents do not report their full valuations vi (·, ·) explicitly but rather their votes

C2.2.quote: every agent submits her most preferred budget decision (x(i) , t(i) )
C2.2.note: Input is a point (allocation in simplex, tax). The paper treats this w.l.o.g. as a direct report of the cardinal type α.

C2.3.quote: Every agent i is associated with a type

C2.4.quote: assume that i falsely reports αi′ ̸= αi
C2.4.note: Votes g(αi) and types αi use separate notation, and misreports are considered.

C3.1.quote: Now, assume that i falsely reports αi′ ̸= αi
C3.1.note: The IC analysis considers misreports; the vanishing-payments analysis evaluates truthful reports only.

C3.2.quote: Since every agent reports (x(i) , t(i) ) = g(αi )

C3.3.quote: truthfully reporting the types forms a Coalition-Proof Nash Equilibrium
C3.3.note: Truthful reporting is justified by the mechanism's SDSIC property.

C4.1.note: C2.2 contains no RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH or PAIR.

C4.2.note: The term appears only in reference titles.

C5.1.quote: designed to maximize the social welfare

C5.2.quote: Assumption 3, however, provides that this is enough to fully recover
C5.2.note: Welfare is defined on valuations of the true types, recovered from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: assume that i falsely reports αi′ ̸= αi
VOT.note: Voters are strategic in the SDSIC analysis and truthful in the payment analysis; no information assumption is stated.

DES.quote_behav: the designer may have some goal in mind that she may
DES.note: The designer's objective is modelled explicitly via the bias function C and ψ, which are chosen exogenously.

C7.1.quote: C(x, t) must be independent of the realization of preferences
C7.1.note: VOT are strategic in the IC analysis of biased mechanisms, while the designer's choice of C is fixed.

C7.2.quote: C(x, t) must be independent of the realization of preferences
C7.2.note: The designer's choice is fixed independently of preferences to maintain incentive compatibility, which is an argument.

C8.1.note: Coalition-Proof Nash Equilibrium (Corollary 2) is used as the coalitional concept.

claims.quote: granting the community with higher control over economic policies
VCG involves monetary transfers among agents, that seems inappropriate
The US-VCG mechanism is welfare-maximizing and strategy-proof

C9.2.quote: it makes more sense to adopt conventional economic assumptions
C9.2.note: The needed assumptions are stated: the utility model, input-to-type recovery (Assumption 3) and incentives via SDSIC.

C1.reason: Theorem 2 (vanishing payments) and Section 5.1 (properties inherited by M̂) establish which mechanisms satisfy which properties, so AX applies alongside SB and WD.

C3.1.reason: Theorem 2 analyses payments under truthful reports without modelling misreports, so not every main analysis is strategic.

C3.2.reason: The paper states in words that agents report g(αi), their type-induced optimum.

C3.3.reason: Truthful reporting in the non-strategic analysis is grounded in the strategyproofness of the mechanism.

C6.DES.reason: Section 5 explicitly models the designer's objective and choice of bias function, so DES is present, with that choice fixed exogenously.

C6.VOT.reason: MIXED is consistent with C3.1 = SOME, and a dominant-strategy definition does not itself state what voters know.

C7.1.reason: In Section 5 voters are strategic while the present designer type is non-strategic.

C7.2.reason: The paper argues that the designer's bias must be fixed independently of preferences to maintain incentive compatibility, which counts as a reason.

C8.1.reason: Besides dominant strategies, the paper formally treats coalition manipulation and CPNE (Definitions 10-11, Corollary 2), so COAL applies.
